source_observations: bhavat is identified as the honorific second-person word
the masculine head forms are bhavan, bhavantau and bhavantah
the masculine remainder is explicitly assigned to the dhimat pattern
the feminine head forms are bhavati, bhavatyau and bhavatyah and the remainder is assigned to nadi
the neuter head forms are bhavat, bhavatii and bhavanti and the remainder is assigned to jagat
the three referenced pattern entries print their own address rows
third-person predicates are required with bhavat and second-person predicates are rejected
bhavan gacchati and bhavati vadati are the source's positive agreement examples
source_policy_decisions: Compose each explicit bhavat gender assignment only with its named pattern's address row.
Keep the nine gender-number keys distinct even where a spelling collides with a finite or unrelated nominal word.
Select third-person predicate agreement for the source's honorific bhavat register and reject second-person agreement only inside that selected policy.
Do not infer accent, literary attestation, social-register universality or a competing commentary priority.

controls.reason: F VOCsg bhavati is nominal address; finite bhavati and other heads retain their owners.
N VOCpl bhavanti is an inflected nominal key; finite and Uṇādi bhavanti remain separate.
The source positively prescribes third person for this honorific use.
